biggestGap: The central test fails outright: 15-fast-flick and 16-slow-cleave are the same fluid in kind — median particle area 26.5 px vs 25.0 px, 0% of blobs elongated in either, and the fast flick is MORE juice-tinted (75.6% of particle pixels at sat>=0.45) than the slow cleave (69.5%) — so stroke speed does not change morphology at all, let alone in the atomise-vs-sheet direction plate-02 demands.

central_test_fast_vs_slow.note: 6% apart in median blob area; the tiny fraction is BACKWARDS (slow has more small particles than fast). Both are 0%-elongated circular billboards (medFill 0.75 = exactly a disc). No film, no fingers, no ligaments, no strings in either.

a_colour.size_tint_relationship: INVERTED — small particles are MORE saturated (0.743) than large ones (0.619). The bar requires the opposite.
a_colour.conclusion: Reference mist sits at sat 0.12-0.19 while its flesh sits at 0.75 (a 4-6x drop). Our mist sits at 0.74 — identical to flesh saturation. The code declares KEY=(1.00,0.945,0.870) (sat 0.13) and mixes white->juice by size class, but no achromatic mist reaches the screen; what is visible is the fat juice-tinted spray class.

b_size_distribution.mode: 33-64 px (29.7% of blobs); 51.6% of all blobs land in 17-64 px
b_size_distribution.conclusion: Our median particle is 26.5 px area vs the reference's 5.2 px-equivalent — 5x the area, 2.3x the diameter. The distribution has a MODE AT MID-SIZE, not a heavy tail toward tiny. Nothing is sub-pixel: the shader's grow=clamp(1.15/pxR,1,4) floor guarantees no droplet can ever be smaller than ~2.3 px across.

c_spray_geometry.conclusion: Not a directed wedge off the cut plane. Every 30-degree sector is populated; the only bias is DOWNWARD (5-8x more particles below the blade than above), i.e. gravity-fed confetti fall spanning ~150 degrees of arc, at only 50 ms after the cut. plate-02's mist is a tight fan hugging the cut plane with a wake behind the blade's trailing edge.

02-cut+33ms.note: 0.04% of frame; visually a single flat pink billboard quad poking out to the right of the melon

sheet_timeline_still_inverted.conclusion: The envelope is monotonically INCREASING through 500 ms. Round 1's inversion peaked at 250 ms; r2's peaks at 500 ms or later. The bar wants full extent by 30-40 ms and gone by ~130 ms, dying by tearing. At +33ms there is effectively no juice at all.

evidence.what_did_move: The r1 frame-flooding regression is fixed — corner luminance on 15-fast-flick went from [0.095, 0.151, 0.101, 0.144] to [0.000, 0.000, 0.000, 0.000], so particles are now legible against a black void instead of drowning in bloom. That is the stage piece's win, not the juice piece's; r1 particle statistics are not comparable because the flood merged the frame into one blob. On every axis this piece owns — speed-dependent morphology, mist colour, size tail, wedge geometry, sheet envelope — the numbers show no movement.
evidence.blind_test: Instant. A field of near-uniform round orange dots with hard edges over black is a particle system; plate-02's aerosol is a near-continuous silver haze of sub-pixel scatterers whose individual grains you cannot count. There is nothing to hesitate over.

fix: In /home/claude/juice/src/juice/fluid.js the intent is coded but never reaches the pixels, for two specific reasons. (1) Line ~1039: `const nSpr = Math.round(q.spray * amtK * (0.50 + 0.60 * mistness) * bk)` makes the FAT, JUICE-TINTED spray budget GROW with mistness — a fast flick emits more of exactly the class that should vanish. Invert it to `(0.95 - 0.75 * fast) * (0.40 + 0.60 * heavy)` so spray/beads collapse as the stroke gets fast, and let mist carry the fast case alone. (2) Line ~348: `vAlpha.assign(pow(grow, -1.2))` under-dims the sub-pixel floor (a disc needs grow^-2 for energy conservation), and `grow = clamp(1.15/pxR, 1.0, 4.0)` at line ~346 hard-floors every droplet at ~2.3 px across, which is why 0% of measured blobs are sub-pixel and 66% are >=16 px. Change to `pow(grow, -2.0)` and drop the mist base radius so pxR lands near 0.3-0.5 px, then raise q.mist so the count compensates. Target, measurable on the next 15-vs-16 pair: fast flick >=80% of particle pixels at sat<0.25 with median blob area <=6 px; slow cleave <=30% achromatic with median blob area >=25 px and >=25% of blobs at aspect>2 (ligaments). Separately, the sheet lifetime at line ~1013 (`A.fB.array[i4+3] = (0.075 + 0.058*filmness) * ...`) is right on paper but the emitted sheet is 101 px at +33 ms and 4471 px at +500 ms — the envelope driving it is running backwards and must be checked against `simT`.
